cohort: 300 pregnant women at term (37-42 weeks gestation) were included, with 150 undergoing induction and 150 experiencing spontaneous labor.
finding: Women in the induced labor group experienced a higher cesarean section rate, longer labor duration, and more frequent postpartum hemorrhage and NICU admissions compared to the spontaneous labor group, while Apgar scores remained comparable.
mod_finding: The induced labor group had a significantly higher cesarean section rate (35%) compared to the spontaneous labor group (18%).
